papers.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
papers.problem: AI agents paste raw tool output into their context, which slows them and hides the facts that matter.
papers.fix: A model that squeezes tool output into compact hidden tokens cuts token use by 70.01% to 89.24% and improves results.
papers.practicalUseCase: If this holds, agent runs get much cheaper and faster, so test context compression before buying a bigger model.
papers.limitation: Tests covered web-search agents on four question benchmarks and two model families only.

papers.title: Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.problem: Offline AI search trusts signed update packs, but a signature does not prove the vectors match the text.
papers.fix: Tampered vectors can drop correct answers from 0.75 to 0.39, and verifying quantisation codes accepted every honest vector tested.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you ship signed knowledge packs, check the vectors against the text, because a signature alone leaves a gap.
papers.limitation: Results come from five corpora, two embedding models, and one Raspberry Pi 5 setup.

papers.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
papers.problem: AI-guided program search runs slowly because the model writes long text reasoning many times each round.
papers.fix: Cheap agent swarms that think in hidden vectors match rival results in 3 to 8 minutes, not 60.
papers.practicalUseCase: Small models can now search for science solutions fast, so try swarm search before paying for a frontier model.
papers.limitation: Tests covered 21 maths and scientific computing problems, so other kinds of tasks are unproven.

papers.title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
papers.problem: No large collection of open research problems existed, so judging AI on real research-level work was hard.
papers.fix: Without web access, AI agents rediscovered at most 7 of 40 solved maths problems; web wins mostly meant lookup.
papers.practicalUseCase: If this holds, treat AI claims of new discoveries with caution, and check whether the answer was simply looked up.
papers.limitation: The benchmark covers maths problems only, and the agent test used a 50-problem high-quality subset.

papers.title: StepX-OPD: Rethinking Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation in Diffusion Models
papers.problem: Image models trained in two stages, first capabilities then few-step speed, score lower once compressed and train slowly.
papers.fix: One merged training stage beats other four-step methods, tops the forty-step model, and uses about 37% fewer GPU-hours on SD3.5-Medium.
papers.practicalUseCase: If this holds, fast image models need fewer training runs, so merge the stages when you train one.
papers.limitation: Tests covered two model families, SD3.5-Medium and FLUX.1-dev, and the GPU saving was measured on SD3.5-Medium only.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Sustainability sukuk are growing, but nobody had measured what drives how big each issue is.
papers.fix: In 11,944 sukuk issues, equity-based contracts and social purposes bring larger issues, while second party opinion costs shrink them.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you plan a sustainability sukuk, favour equity-based contracts and weigh second party opinion costs against issue size.
papers.limitation: The data stop at 2022, and the study shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks set up sustainability committees, but it was unclear whether they lead to real green action.
papers.fix: Committees raise environmental scores in both bank types, but in Islamic banks the effect looks symbolic, not substantive.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you judge a bank's green claims, look for green products and innovation, not just a committee.
papers.limitation: The study covers emerging-market banks only and shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan lacked evidence on whether AI and big data improve competitiveness and sustainable development.
papers.fix: AI use, big data skills, and data management all link to better competitiveness and sustainable development in Jordanian Islamic banks.
papers.practicalUseCase: If this holds, banks should invest in AI and data practices, since staff digital skills did not lift sustainable development.
papers.limitation: The survey is cross-sectional, covers 214 managers in Jordan only, and shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: It was unclear which factors drive bank growth in countries that run Islamic and conventional banks side by side.
papers.fix: ICT adoption drives growth most across 218 banks in 12 countries, and high-tech exports help only alongside ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: If this holds, banks and regulators should fund digital infrastructure first, because high-tech exports alone did not help.
papers.limitation: Data cover 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, and the study shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Procrastination among US college students: Prevalence and impact relative to common health and life issues
papers.problem: Nobody knew how common student procrastination is, or how it compares with other health and life problems.
papers.fix: Procrastination affected 72.3% of 65,950 US students, and hurt grades for 45.4%, which is 3.5 times more than ADHD.
papers.practicalUseCase: If this holds, treat procrastination as a top problem, because it harms performance more than money worries or ADHD.
papers.limitation: Students reported their own problems in one US survey, so the data show links, not cause.

papers.title: “The significance of context”: Fit, friction, and function in the work lives of early career academics with ADHD
papers.problem: Little was known about how early-career academics with ADHD experience building a career.
papers.fix: Academia can reward ADHD traits, but social and institutional pressure often blocks that, according to interviews with early-career academics.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you have ADHD, pick workplaces that fit your style, because fit decides whether your traits help or hurt.
papers.limitation: This interview study is qualitative, so it shows personal experience, not how common these patterns are.
